title: World Airways Flight 802

agencies.name: National Transportation Safety Board
agencies.report_title: Aircraft Accident Report: World Airways Flight 802, Douglas DC-8-63CF

summary: World Airways Flight 802, a Douglas DC-8-63CF cargo aircraft, struck Mount Dutton at 3,500 feet near Cold Bay Airport, Alaska, during an instrument approach. The aircraft had strayed significantly off-course into an area of poor radio navigation coverage. All six crew members were killed. The NTSB found the captain failed to adhere to published instrument approach procedures.
probable_cause: The captain's non-adherence to published instrument approach procedures for Cold Bay Airport, resulting in descent below safe altitude while off-course. Contributing factors included weather conditions and inadequate radio navigation reception in the area.

factors.evidence: Aircraft strayed significantly off-course into area of poor radio navigation reception (p. 3)
Aircraft descended in clouds toward Cold Bay Airport (p. 3)
Captain did not adhere to published instrument approach procedures (p. 3)
Aircraft struck Mount Dutton at 3,500 feet altitude (p. 3)

events.text: Flight 802 cruising from Travis AFB toward Clark AB after uneventful flight
Descent initiated toward Cold Bay Airport
Captain began instrument approach to Cold Bay Airport
Aircraft strayed significantly off-course into area of poor radio navigation reception while in clouds
Continued descent while off-course, not following published approach procedures
Aircraft struck Mount Dutton at altitude of 3,500 feet

recommendations.text: Improve radio navigation coverage and procedures for approaches to remote airfields
Standardize instrument approach procedures and enforcement of adherence
